excerpt: Squint uses AI and augmented reality to turn factory workers' know-how into step-by-step guides on a phone or tablet. It raised a $40M Series B in 2025.
content:
Squint is a software company that helps manufacturers capture and share how expert workers do their jobs. A worker records a task, such as changing over a packaging line or servicing a machine, and Squint's AI documents it automatically as a step-by-step procedure. Other workers then follow that guide on a phone or tablet, with augmented reality placing instructions over the equipment in front of them, and AI agents give real-time guidance to cut errors. Squint now describes its product as industrial intelligence, and its website lists uses in quality and scrap reduction, maintenance and uptime, standardisation and compliance, and workforce training, across automotive, food and beverage, consumer goods, oil and gas, energy and heavy industry.

Devin Bhushan, a former Splunk executive, founded the company and is its CEO. In an interview with Fortune he said the company's biggest competitor is physical binders of paper procedures. SiliconANGLE reported that PepsiCo uses Squint in bottling and packaging plants and said training times were cut in half, and that Michelin uses it to standardise complex assembly across its plants; Manufacturing Today also named Ford as a customer.

Funding

On 12 August 2025 Squint announced a $40 million Series B co-led by The Westly Group and TCV, with earlier investors Sequoia Capital and Menlo Ventures taking part. Fortune reported a $265 million valuation, and SiliconANGLE put total funding at more than $59 million. The company said it would use the money to improve its AI and expand into industries such as energy and logistics.

Pricing

Squint does not publish prices. Its website asks companies to book a demo.

Who it suits

Squint fits operations, quality and training leaders at plants that depend on experienced staff and paper-based procedures. It is less relevant to office businesses or very small workshops.

We have not tested Squint. This page is based on Squint's website and on Fortune, SiliconANGLE and Manufacturing Today.
